title: drogna query layer configuration
description: C-09's one configuration file. Everything the query layer knows about where things are arrives here: the coverage store root and the names within it, the observation store connection and the tables it projects, the public base URL the served links are built from, and the response limits that keep the droplet answering. Nothing in query/ carries a literal path, host or port, so a value absent from this document is a startup failure rather than a default nobody chose.

public_base_url.description: The address this service is reached at from outside, used to build every self and navigation link it serves. It is the destination's advertised address, never the container's.

bind.description: The listener. Separate from the public base URL because a container binds one address and is reached at another.

collection_prefix.description: The one path prefix every collection sits under. Prefix-based default-deny at the reverse proxy (FR-040, FR-041) works only if adding a collection cannot change the shape of the path space, so this is a single value and not a per-collection one.

coverage_store.title: Coverage store layout
coverage_store.description: The naming convention of C-08, as values rather than as constants in source. stores/coverage/layout.md is the normative account of what these names mean and what a publisher must do with them; the values are here because Constitution IV admits no filename in component source, and because the two destinations must be able to prove they use the same ones.

root.description: Directory the store is rooted at, read-only to this service.

runs_dirname.description: Directory beneath the root holding one directory per run.

staging_dirname.description: Directory beneath the root a run is assembled in before it is visible. It is inside the store, and therefore on the store's volume, because the publisher makes a run visible by renaming it out of here into runs_dirname and a rename between two volumes is a copy, which is not indivisible. Nothing beneath it is ever catalogued or served.

current_pointer.description: File at the root naming the current run, one identifier per line. Exactly one line resolves; more than one is the conflict FR-016 requires be refused rather than resolved.

forecast_file.description: The forecast field within a run directory.

uncertainty_file.description: The uncertainty field within a run directory.

manifest_file.description: The run manifest within a run directory; its presence is what makes a run complete.

partial_suffix.description: Suffix a publisher writes under before renaming into place. Anything carrying it is invisible to the catalogue, which is how a partially written run is never served.

run_id.title: Run identifier derivation
run_id.description: Run identifiers are a pure function of the root seed and the run sequence, so a replayed scenario produces the same catalogue (Constitution II, FR-013). The rule is named and versioned rather than described, because this feature and the publisher must agree without sharing code.

version.description: A change here changes every identifier.

coverage.title: What a coverage run holds
coverage.description: The axis names and the parameters served. Named here because the coverage output is a genuine port and a later implementation may spell its axes differently; nothing in the provider assumes a spelling.

parameters.description: Forecast parameters and the uncertainty parameter together, as FR-002 requires: one collection, not two that could disagree.

name.description: How the parameter is addressed in a query.

variable.description: The variable's name inside the coverage file.

source.description: Which of a run's two fields the variable is read from.

unit.description: Unit symbol, as CoverageJSON reports it.

label.description: One line for a person reading the collection.

standard_name.description: CF standard name where one exists. Absent where CF has none; a plausible invention would be a claim the vocabulary does not support.

observations.title: Observation store projection
observations.description: Where the observations schema is and what the SensorThings entity set is projected from. Table and column names are values because the schema belongs to C-06 and this service only reads it, with select permission and nothing more.

dsn.description: Connection string for the select-only role.

schema.description: The database schema the entity set is projected from.

role.description: The role connected as. It holds select permission only (FR-011); the assertion is a test, not a comment.

tables.description: One table per served entity set. Locations and HistoricalLocations have no entry, deliberately: see query/conformance.md.

limits.title: Response limits
limits.description: The droplet is small and a response that cannot be produced is worse than one that is refused. Every limit here is named in the refusal that enforces it (FR-020).

interpolation.title: How a value between grid nodes is arrived at
interpolation.description: Stated rather than assumed. The spike measured half a degree of avoidable error between interpolating in time and snapping to the nearest step, and neither is distinguishable from outside the response.

method.description: Linear in longitude, latitude, depth and time.

out_of_domain.description: One value, and an enumeration all the same, because the alternative has to be visible as a decision that was not taken. A forecast horizon that silently extends itself is the worst failure available to this component.

default_depth_metres.description: The depth a trajectory vertex is taken at when its geometry carries no Z ordinate. Explicit, because the spike found the default invisible from outside.

presentation.title: What the served metadata says about who is serving it
presentation.description: pygeoapi requires a provider, a licence and a base map of every deployment. They are destination values rather than constants because a second destination that quietly served a different licence would be exactly the drift NFR-06 exists to catch.

map_tile_url.description: Base map tiles for pygeoapi's own HTML views. A URL, and therefore a destination value.

domain.title: The scenario's envelope
domain.description: The extent every collection is advertised over. It is the scenario's domain, from the destination configuration, and not a list of what the store happens to hold: enumerating runs in configuration is what FR-017 forbids. A run's own extent is in its manifest and is what a query is actually answered against.

bbox.description: Minimum longitude, minimum latitude, maximum longitude, maximum latitude.

vertical.description: Shallowest and deepest depth in metres, positive down.

temporal.description: Simulation time, as ISO-8601 UTC strings. Not host time, and no format keyword: a schema that invited a consumer to fill this from a host clock would have undone Constitution I before any code was written.
